propositions: A verified ticket description write (14,997 chars) was silently reverted to an older revision (10,582 chars) while the ticket's plan-review was in flight, with no error or conflict signal reported.

Optimistic concurrency did not reject the losing write; read-back verification passed immediately after the write, yet the data was later lost, invalidating the documented conflict detection protection.
A subsequent read-modify-write by the agent grafted new edits onto the stale reverted text, corrupting an acceptance criterion by splicing unrelated fragments.

The concurrent interaction between edit and in-flight review-plan emitting sidecar events on the same ticket causes store reconvergence that allows last-writer-wins clobbering of newer description content with stale client-held text.
